in_text_mentions: On the other hand, cephalometric or lateral skull radiography is indicated to evaluate facial growth, paranasal sinuses, hard palate and trauma. The radiographic characteristics of CCD that can be observed in this type of radiography are hypoplasia of the maxillary bone with multiple retained and supernumerary teeth, lack of development of the mastoid cells, and prominence of the frontal and occipital bone, in addition to the type of occlusion and profile of these patients 17 (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Three-dimensional CT reconstruction from a disease-focused case series visibly demonstrates the captioned nonerupted dentition, supported by the article text as supernumerary and nonerupted teeth characteristic of cleidocranial dysplasia. B: The 3D CT skull reconstruction directly demonstrates multiple Wormian bones, a specific recognized manifestation of cleidocranial dysplasia. C: The oblique 3D CT reconstruction shows the captioned zygomatic arch defect and lack of articulation with the malar bone in this cleidocranial dysplasia case. This named manifestation is absent from the supplied vocabulary and is proposed as a short clinical finding. D: The opposite oblique 3D CT reconstruction demonstrates the captioned zygomatic arch defect and lack of articulation with the malar bone in this cleidocranial dysplasia case. This named manifestation is absent from the supplied vocabulary and is proposed as a short clinical finding.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Clinical photograph of the index patient with CCD showing characteristic craniofacial features and sloping shoulders with arrows indicating bilateral shoulder girdle muscle atrophy. b: Chest radiograph demonstrates the captioned absent right clavicle and hypoplastic left clavicle, a classic CCD manifestation. c: Skull radiographs show wormian bones and the captioned hypoplastic maxilla, supporting cleidocranial dysplasia. d: Spine radiograph demonstrates mild scoliosis of the thoraco-lumbar spine as captioned in this CCD case; scoliosis is recorded as a proposed finding because it is absent from the supplied vocabulary.
